articles.title: Google Translate could soon get its own version of Gboard’s Rambler
articles.summary: TL;DR Google introduced Rambler for Gboard earlier this year, removing filler words and cleaning up your voice input for text conversion. Now Google Translate appears to be preparing its own similar mode called Smart assist. It’s not yet clear if Smart assist would have some of the same limitations as Rambler. Voice-to-text sounds like a great idea… until you actually listen closely to how people really speak. While we expect the written word to be clear and formal, speech is often anything but — and that’s exactly why we have tools like Rambler in Gboard , able to compensate for our messy utterances. Now Google Translate looks like it could be cooking up a similar system of its own. You’re reading an Authority Insights story. Authority Insights brings you all the latest exclusive reports,

articles.summary: TL;DR The steps to find the hidden Glowbar Disco app on Googlebooks have been revealed. The app is tucked away in the system settings, but it’s easy enough to find when you know where to look. Glowbar Disco lets you customize the laptop’s light strip with colors, animations, and music-sync effects. The Glowbar is one of the more distinctive features of the new Googlebooks , adding a splash of color to the lid while also serving practical purposes, such as indicating battery status and Gemini activity. But Google has also given it a party trick in the form of a hidden Glowbar Disco app. We learned about the app a couple of weeks ago , but Google didn’t reveal how to access it at the time. articles.title: Microsoft 365 is making a big cut to your OneDrive storage perk
articles.summary: TL;DR Microsoft is cutting the total OneDrive storage for Microsoft 365 Family and Premium subscribers from 6TB to a shared 2TB pool. Solo subscribers could benefit from the change, but families using more than 2TB may need to delete files, move data, or pay for additional storage. The new limits apply immediately to new subscribers, while existing customers will see the change after their first renewal on or after May 2, 2027. Microsoft is taking away one of the biggest perks that came with subscribing to its Microsoft 365 Family or Premium plan . I personally do not have a subscription, though I have thought about paying for one in the past. articles.title: Kubernetes on cgroup v1 is dead. Here’s what comes next.
articles.summary: Welcome back to another edition of Road to KubeCon , where we’re tracking the latest movements in the cloud-native ecosystem as we prepare for KubeCon + CloudNativeCon North America 2026 , happening November 9-12 in Salt Lake City, Utah. In this edition, we consider what happens when compute workloads need to run AI on the edge. Underlying Kubernetes mechanics change, as do observability practices and security decisions. We take a look at the emerging tactics and how a couple of key projects are responding to these changes. articles.title: Surveillance Pricing May Be Coming to a Store Near You
articles.summary: What if the electronic shelf label you see at the grocery store isn't just showing you the price of the jar of mayonnaise you're about to buy — but actually raising the price because you put a can of tuna in your cart. It's called surveillance pricing and retailers like Walmart appear to be locking down technology that will help them figure out how much they can charge you. Bloomberg's Brad Stone joins Stacey Vanek Smith and Max Chafkin on the Everybody's Business podcast to unpack this pricing strategy (which Walmart has denied using). (Source: Bloomberg)

Bloomberg's Brad Stone joins Stacey Vanek Smith and Max Chafkin on the Everybody's Business podcast to unpack this pricing strategy (which Walmart has denied using). (Source: Bloomberg)

articles.title: Neanderthal wooden tools from Spain found preserved in stone
articles.summary: The Stone Age owes its name to tools that survived to our time. The material early humans worked with most, though, was probably wood because it is so much easier to process. Unfortunately, we know very little about Paleolithic woodwork because wood rots relatively quickly. But at Abric Romaní, a rock shelter in Capellades, west of Barcelona, mineral-rich water coated wooden Neanderthal tools in a limestone-like crust. When wood rotted away, it left behind hollow molds that faithfully reflect its shape. In a recent Science Advances study, a team of Spanish archaeologists has cataloged 597 wooden remains from Neanderthal living areas dating from 62,000 to 40,000 years ago. articles.summary: Ukrainian drone strikes have knocked out two of five data centers belonging to the Russian tech giant Yandex. articles.title: A Cray-1 supercomputer replica from 30 "obsolete" Mac Minis
articles.summary: The Museo de Historia de la Computación in Spain has unveiled a 1:1 scale visual replica of the famous Cray-1 supercomputer from 1976. Instead of sourcing expensive, cutting-edge tech to run the system, the creative team powered the project with 30 2012-era Mac Minis. Developed over 18 months, the project serves as a 50th-anniversary tribute to the Cray-1 and Apple's founding. Mac Minis from over a decade ago might not seem like the obvious first choice for building a cluster supercomputer, but when networked together, the developers can orchestrate the 64 active processing cores into a combined 1.3 teraflops of performance in their most recent tests. articles.title: What's been driving Hawaii's lava fountains?
articles.summary: In most cases, hotspot-driven volcanism is relatively sedate, with lava flowing down mountainsides slowly enough that people can walk out of its way. But in a number of locations—Mount Etna, Hawaii, Iceland—lava gets expelled in dramatic fountains that can reach several hundred meters in height. Right now, we're not sure what powers them. However, thanks to a recent set of eruptions at the Kilauea volcano, we have some of the best documentation yet of erupting lava fountains. In a recent edition of Science, researchers from the US Geological Survey describe what we've seen and compare it with what we might expect based on our best ideas about what powers these fountains of molten rock. articles.title: AI coding agents generate more code, but not more software
articles.summary: Anyone who has even tangentially associated with computer programming knows that modern AI coding assistants and agents can be incredibly efficient at generating huge amounts of functional code . But coders making use of those tools also know better than to trust the accuracy of that code , meaning substantial effort needs to be spent reviewing any AI-generated output. A recent study of actual coding practices across hundreds of firms finds that human code review forms a significant "bottleneck" for the overall efficiency of AI coding tools, resulting in "little evidence that firms increase software output or reduce employment" by using them. articles.summary: Outrage has erupted among health experts over news that the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention is still eager to fund a widely condemned vaccine trial that would expose newborns in Guinea-Bissau to hepatitis B, putting them at high risk of a lifelong infection, which can lead to liver cirrhosis, liver cancer, and premature death. articles.summary:
過去一年，「代理式AI」（Agentic AI）成了科技圈熱門關鍵字。從協助寫程式的自動化助手，到能自主處理郵件、管理檔案，甚至代為執行系統指令的智慧代理，這些工具正快速走進企業日常運作，成為員工桌面與伺服器環境中的新住戶。
